definition: Argument mining, or argumentation mining, is a research area within the natural language processing field.
details: The goal of argument mining is the automatic extraction and identification of argumentative structures from natural language text with the aid of computer programs. Such argumentative structures include the premise, conclusions, the argument scheme and the relationship between the main and subsidiary argument, or the main and counter-argument within discourse. The Argument Mining workshop series is the main research forum for argument mining related research.

explainer.lead: Argument mining uses computer programs to turn ordinary text into an explicit map of an argument. It identifies premises and conclusions, then represents how supporting and opposing arguments relate to one another.

tiers.eli5: Imagine highlighting the reasons and the main point in a class debate, then drawing arrows between them. Argument mining teaches a computer to do something similar with written text. It can also notice when one argument answers or challenges another.
tiers.practitioner: An application takes natural-language text as input and produces argumentative structure: premises, conclusions, argument schemes, and discourse relations. Outputs may connect a main argument to subsidiary arguments or counter-arguments. A key pitfall is treating the task as isolated span classification when the relationships between components are also part of the target structure.
tiers.paperLevel: Given natural-language discourse D, argument mining infers an argumentative structure A = (P, C, S, R), where P denotes premises, C conclusions, S argument schemes, and R relations among arguments. R includes main-to-subsidiary and main-to-counter-argument relations within discourse. The task is automatic extraction and identification of these structures by computer programs.

explainer.example: For the text “We should extend library hours because many students study after dinner. Although longer hours cost money, the benefit to students justifies the expense,” the output can mark “many students study after dinner” as a premise and “we should extend library hours” as a conclusion. The cost concern introduces a counter-argument, while the final clause supports the main argument against it.

explainer.intuition: A written argument is more than a collection of sentences: some statements give reasons, some state conclusions, and others support or oppose the main argument. Argument mining makes that hidden organization explicit.
howItWorks: Provide natural-language discourse to a computer program.
Identify text that expresses premises and conclusions.
Determine the argument scheme connecting them.
Output the components and their discourse relationships.
explainer.whyItMatters: It converts argumentative discourse into a structured representation rather than leaving reasons and conclusions buried in prose. That representation captures both the parts of an argument and the ways arguments support or oppose one another.
misconceptions: It is not merely finding individual opinions.
It extracts argument structure rather than deciding whether claims are true.
Relations between arguments matter, not just premises and conclusions.
